classification.difficultyReason: Combine adjacent angles at the pole before applying the cosine rule.

content.prompt: A pole $OV$ is held in position by two ropes, $VA$ and $VB$. The ground attachment points $A$, $O$ and $B$ lie on a straight level line, with $O$ between $A$ and $B$. If $VA=6\text{ m}$, $VB=6.5\text{ m}$, $\angle OVB=32^\circ$ and $\angle OVA=27^\circ$, find the distance $AB$, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: User-approved correction: OV is a leaning pole on straight level ground through A, O and B; ropes retain lengths6m and6.5m and angles27degrees and32degrees to OV.
spec.mathematics: O lies between A and B. Coordinates are a rigid rotation of the exact rope triangle, making ground AB horizontal while OV leans; all original numerical givens and the6.2m answer are preserved.

answer.worked:
The ropes lie on opposite sides of the pole, so their included angle is the sum of the two given angles. Apply the cosine rule in $\triangle AVB$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle AVB&=27^\circ+32^\circ\\\angle AVB&=59^\circ\\AB^2&=6^2+6.5^2-2\times6\times6.5\cos59^\circ\\AB&=\sqrt{6^2+6.5^2-2\times6\times6.5\cos59^\circ}\\AB&\approx6.2\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
